title: Reference-data client artefact coordinates, the cache time-to-live catalog entry, the refresh rule with no change event and the client-to-kit boundary are not specified
source: Legacy RWB-E1-043 sections 3, 12, 13 and 14; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 20, 27, 29 and 44; Temporal and Drools design slide 15; Ownership Map v1 (reference_version, reference_row and lov_value owned by P3; rule_package, rule_package_version, rule_row and rule_test_case owned by P7)
section: 3 Preconditions; 8 Business rules; 12.2 REST operations consumed; 12.7 Tables owned; 13 Solution plan; 18 Traceability
description: No source fixes five values this library deliverable needs. (a) The artefact coordinates of the platform library — the group, the artefact name and the publication channel — are stated nowhere; the legacy module was a folder inside the one deployable. (b) The cache time to live is named as `refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` = 300 (assumed; DL11) in the legacy configuration service, and no technical specification gives the catalog entry that now carries it in the rwb-case parameter catalog. (c) The refresh rule is fixed only by the absence of a change event: the legacy design publishes none for a version change, the target names no reference event for rwb-case on Architecture v5 slides 14 and 20, and Architecture v5 slide 20 lists only AccessPolicyChanged, DoaLimitChanged and RulePackageInForce as cache-refresh events, so how a consumer learns of a newly approved version is a read on expiry and nothing more. (d) The boundary between this client and the embedded rules kit is described in prose only: the kit fetches rule models from rwb-decision (DP-04) and the client reads reference data from rwb-case (DP-07), and no document states which of the two answers a caller that needs both, or how a rule package code is refused at the client. (e) The BRD section of REQ-CWC-016 is not in the legacy traceability table, which lists only REQ-DRI-011 and REQ-CWC-006 although section 8 BR7 cites the logging requirement.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-043 section 12 (published interfaces in recovery.casewf.refdata.api, no artefact coordinates), section 13 (`refdata.cache.ttl-seconds` = 300, assumed; DL11) and section 14 (message catalogue); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 20 (every service from the service template and shared libraries; the event list that refreshes a cache) and slide 29 (one schema and one login per service, boundary test in every build); Temporal and Drools design slide 15 (governance central in rwb-decision, services hold an evaluated copy); Ownership Map rulings on reference_version, reference_row, lov_value, rule_package and rule_package_version; no technical specification exists for the platform shared libraries.
owner_role: Platform team (PLT) architect with the rwb-case and rwb-decision owners
proposed: Take the artefact coordinates and the publication channel from the platform library baseline (RWB-PLT-TPL) and record them there, not in this story; publish the cache time to live as a named entry of the rwb-case parameter catalog with 300 as its documented default; keep the refresh on cache expiry and add no event, raising the contract to a new version if the rwb-case owner later publishes one through the inbox library; put the kit boundary in a contract test that refuses a rule package code and asserts that no rule row reaches the client; record the BRD section of REQ-CWC-016 when the Epic 1 BRD next version is produced.

title: The published reference-data client contract, the version and row data contract, the LOV-REF-TABLE code list and the no-version failure surface are not specified in a technical specification
source: Legacy RWB-E1-043 sections 7, 8 BR1, 9, 12 and 14; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 11, 14 and 29; Temporal and Drools design slide 15; Ownership Map v1
section: 1 Story; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12.1 to 12.9 Contract; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages
description: The legacy story publishes the two interfaces and the two records inside recovery.casewf.refdata.api and describes them in prose; no technical specification turns them into a published contract. Four values are therefore open. (a) The published client surface: the three method signatures, their parameter names and the exception type are legacy Java and not a frozen artefact with a version and a deprecation rule. (b) The version and row data contract: the legacy field identifiers DF-REF-159 to DF-REF-171 and DF-REF-181 to DF-REF-184 exist in the Logical Data Model, and no source states which of them the wire projection carries, in which order, or how a row is projected from row_data. (c) The LOV-REF-TABLE code list: the twelve codes are named in legacy section 8 BR1 and no source states that the list is the contract's code set, that a rule package code is absent from it, or that the holiday calendar has no code. (d) The no-version failure surface: MSG-P3-027 is fixed for the refusal, and no source states whether the client throws a checked exception, what the payload of the failure carries, or how a caller without Reference data R is answered.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E1-043 section 12 (the two interfaces and two records, and the sentence that rows throws NoVersionInForceException), section 8 BR1 (the twelve codes and the two exclusions), section 9 (VALIDATED, APPROVED, ROLLED_BACK) and section 14 (MSG-P3-027); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 11 (OpenAPI 3.1, one hop, 2 s timeout, RFC 9457 problem details, contract tests in every build), slide 14 (rwb-case owns the reference data) and slide 29 (boundary test); Temporal and Drools design slide 15 (the rule registry stays central); Ownership Map rulings on reference_version, reference_row, lov_value and the rule tables; no technical specification exists for the platform shared libraries.
owner_role: Platform team (PLT) contract owner with the rwb-case owner
proposed: Publish the client surface as one versioned contract artefact at major version 1, carrying the legacy methods and records as they stand; publish the version and row projection from the legacy field identifiers with the three-value status vocabulary; fix the code set as the twelve LOV-REF-TABLE codes with the rule-package and holiday exclusions as testable sentences; publish the refusal as a checked exception carrying MSG-P3-027, the table code and the business date, non-retryable, with the caller's 403 surfaced by the access guard library.
